summary: Jerome Point light at the entrance to St. Peter's Canal, Cape Breton: lit 1883, rebuilt 1956, unwatched since 1965. Seasonal light; tower closed, park open in season.

structures.note: First tower: square pyramidal with a two-storey dwelling attached on the landward side (LighthouseFriends). Replaced in 1956.
Built 1956 with a detached keeper's dwelling; both connected to commercial power (LighthouseFriends). Coast Guard list: 10.9 m.

staffing.note: De-staffed May 1960 after a temporary keeper; caretaker to 1962; made unwatched in 1965 with an automatic changer and sun switch (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Park and grounds open in season; the tower is closed. LighthouseFriends: park open mid-June to mid-October. Rowlett: site and park open mid June to mid September. Accessible by paved road with parking.

events.note: Lawrence J. O'Toole began work on the lighthouse under a $1,300 contract
John D. Matheson hired as first keeper at $200 a year
Six pole lights built along the route to the canal: three in Lennox Passage, three in St. Peter's Inlet
Pilley's mechanical hand fog alarm given to the keeper, to sound in answer to steamers' whistles
Seventh-order dioptric lens and a hand fog horn (NSLPS)
Fog signal in answer to vessels (NSLPS)
Wooden square pyramidal tower almost 11 m, with a detached keeper's dwelling, both on commercial power
De-staffed May 1960 after a temporary keeper; caretaker hired until 1962
Keeper's dwelling and lighthouse property deeded to the canal authority
Made unwatched after an automatic changer and a sun switch were installed

notes_for_editor: Keeper conflict, not resolved: LighthouseFriends gives James McAskill at Jerome Point, 1897 to 1913. The Department's lists of 1902 ('McAskill, Kenneth Jerome Point'), 1909 (Kenneth McAskill, appointed 30 July 1901, $320) and 1911 ('Jerome Point Kenneth McAskill July 30') name Kenneth. The 1909 table is cited here as the 1909 report, printed 1910 (scan 167, printed 160). The 1909 entry is on one OCR line with name, date and salary; the station is not printed on that line and comes from the 1911 pairing (scan 244). Ownership conflict: LighthouseFriends and Rowlett say Coast Guard; NSLPS says Government of Canada; LighthouseFriends says the dwelling and property went to the canal authority in 1963. Current owner not verified. Season conflict: LighthouseFriends says the park is open mid-June to mid-October, Rowlett says mid-June to mid-September; the Coast Guard list calls the light seasonal, while the record says 'active'. Height conflict for the 1956 tower: LighthouseFriends almost 11 m; Coast Guard list 10.9 m; Rowlett 10.5 m (35 ft); all stated. Matheson's 1883 appointment and the McNeil/Barron/Sampson keeper dates are from LighthouseFriends only; not checked in the Department lists read. Parks Canada's St. Peters Canal page was searched and yielded nothing usable. No Chronicling America search was made for this station. Record photo (Wikimedia Commons) not checked.
